evidence:
frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:105-106,125-126 — the auth-gating component hardcodes four user-facing English strings with no react-i18next: aria-label="Checking authentication" and Loading... in the loading branch, and

Access Denied

+

You do not have permission to access this page.

in the role-denied branch. The app ships sk/cs/de/en, so a non-English user who is authenticated-but-underprivileged sees an English-only Access Denied page.

This is the only fully-hardcoded auth surface in the pages/+components/ segment: the sibling AuthRequiredGate.tsx (same directory, same purpose) already renders t('errors.authenticationRequired') / t('errors.missingOrgContext') / t('auth.signIn'), and LoginPage.tsx / AuthCallbackPage.tsx are fully i18n'd. Fix: import useTranslation and wrap the four strings (reuse the existing errors.* / auth.* keys where they exist).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/OfflineIndicator.tsx — the component never imports useTranslation and hardcodes two user-facing banner strings: line 58-60 "You are offline. Some features may be unavailable." and line 89 "Connection restored". Both are surfaced via role="alert"/role="status" live regions, so screen readers announce untranslated English to sk/cs/de users.

Consistent i18n gap with the ProtectedRoute finding — every other rendered component under components/ that shows copy (Toast, ConnectionStatus, PageLoading, LanguageSwitcher, ErrorBoundary) already calls useTranslation. Fix: add useTranslation and move the two strings into the offline/* or common/* i18n namespace.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:122-129 — the role-denied branch renders a bare
with only an

/

and no recovery affordance: no link back to the dashboard/home, no 'switch account' or 'request access' action, and (because ProtectedRoute wraps route element content) no app chrome/nav. A user who reaches a role-gated route via a stale bookmark or a shared deep link is dead-ended with only the browser back button.

Contrast the sibling AuthRequiredGate.tsx, which provides a <Link to="/login"> recovery path in its equivalent error-page block. Completeness gap: give the Access Denied state at least one navigation affordance (e.g. <Link to="/">back to dashboard</Link>) so authenticated-but-underprivileged users are not stranded.
